We teach three core techniques on HSMA: **discrete event simulation**, **geographic modelling and optimisation**, and **machine learning**.

Each of the playgrounds below gives you a quick, hands-on taste of one of them, built around a realistic healthcare problem. There's nothing to install and no code to write - everything runs in your web browser.

The first time you open a playground, it can take a little while to load while your browser downloads everything it needs to run the model.

::: {.playground-card .neon-tile .neon-tile--blue}

```{=html}
<div class="tile-header"><span class="prompt" aria-hidden="true">&gt; </span>Discrete Event Simulation</div>
```

[*"I want to fix my delays, and see what works before I try it"*]{.playground-question}

Discrete event simulation lets you build a computer model of a pathway - like patients arriving at an emergency department, queuing, and being seen - and then try out changes such as adding staff or altering processes in a safe environment before you make them for real.

In this playground, you can change how a department is resourced, run the simulation, and watch the queues build up (or disappear!) in an animated view of the pathway.

```{=html}
<div class="tile-header"><span class="prompt" aria-hidden="true">&gt; </span>Geographic Modelling</div>
```

[*"Where is demand, and where should I put my services?"*]{.playground-question}

Geographic modelling helps you understand where the need for a service is, how long it takes people to reach it, and where new sites should go to balance priorities like travel time, fair access for everyone, and cost.

In this playground, you get to decide where a new diagnostic centre should go, see how your choice affects travel times across the area, and compare your picks with those found by an optimisation algorithm.

```{=html}
<div class="tile-header"><span class="prompt" aria-hidden="true">&gt; </span>Machine Learning</div>
```

[*"I want to identify patients to target with interventions"*]{.playground-question}

Machine learning models learn patterns from past data so that they can make predictions about the future - such as which patients are most likely to miss an upcoming appointment - helping services target their interventions where they will make the biggest difference.

In this playground, you can see how a model predicts missed appointments, explore which factors drive its predictions, and compare targeting reminder calls using the model against simpler approaches - including a rule of your own.

## Want to learn more?

If you work in health or social care and want to learn to use these techniques yourself, take a look at [HSMA 7](hsma7.qmd), our free 15-month training and mentoring programme.

If you're a leader or decision maker who wants to understand what these techniques can do for your organisation without writing any code, our [HSMA-λ workshops](lambda.qmd) may be a better fit.

```{=html}
<script>
document.querySelectorAll(".playground-load").forEach(function (button) {
  button.addEventListener("click", function () {
    var frame = button.closest(".playground-frame");
    if (!frame || frame.classList.contains("is-loaded")) return;
    var iframe = document.createElement("iframe");
    iframe.src = button.dataset.src;
    iframe.title = button.dataset.title;
    iframe.setAttribute("allow", "fullscreen");
    frame.textContent = "";
    frame.appendChild(iframe);
    frame.classList.add("is-loaded");
  });
});
</script>
```
